quiz.q: Which of these is NOT part of the work you send for this capstone?
quiz.explain: Packaging comes much later. This capstone asks for screenshots, a map and a writeup.

quiz.q: How do you get a clean top-down map of the courtyard?
choices: Switch the viewport to Top (orthographic) and screenshot it
quiz.explain: Orthographic Top has no perspective distortion, so routes and sizes read true.

quiz.q: What makes the three routes count as three?
choices: They differ in a clear way, like length, risk, height or cover
quiz.explain: A route only counts if choosing it changes something for the player.

quiz.q: The goal is hard to find in the Lighting Only view. What do you redo?
choices: The names of the Material Instances
quiz.explain: The goal should be the brightest point. Fix the lighting before adding detail.

quiz.q: Which bookmarks does the capstone ask for?
choices: Entrance, a mid-route point, and the goal
quiz.explain: Three fixed views let a reviewer judge the space the way you did.

quiz.q: Where do you read Max Walk Speed and Jump Z Velocity?
choices: The Character Movement component on your character Blueprint
quiz.explain: Character Movement holds walking, jumping and falling settings.

quiz.q: The default Third Person capsule has a half-height of 96. How tall is the capsule?
quiz.explain: Half-height is measured from the center, so double it. Check your own template's values.

quiz.q: What does Max Step Height control?
choices: The tallest ledge the character walks up without jumping
quiz.explain: Anything taller needs a jump. Size stairs and curbs with this in mind.

quiz.q: Why measure jump distance in a metrics gym instead of calculating it?
choices: Air control, gravity and friction all affect it, so testing gives the number players actually get
The gym is required to package
quiz.explain: Test in PIE and record what works, then leave some margin.

quiz.q: Why make the sheet shareable?
choices: So you don't need to test
So everyone building for the character uses the same numbers and kit pieces fit
quiz.explain: A metrics sheet is a team document. In later quests it becomes part of the kit you hand to others.

quiz.q: Which key toggles the navigation display in the viewport?
quiz.explain: P shows the NavMesh. Green means AI can walk there.

quiz.q: Why is there a gap in the green along every wall?
choices: The navmesh is pulled in by the agent radius so AI doesn't clip into walls
quiz.explain: Tight doorways can close up completely. That's a metrics issue.

quiz.q: AI MoveTo goes straight to On Fail. What do you check first?
choices: Whether the pawn and the destination are both on the green navmesh
quiz.explain: No path, no move. Also check the pawn is possessed by an AI Controller (placed Characters are by default).

quiz.q: A closed door should block AI, and opening it should let them through. What's needed?
choices: Runtime Generation set to Dynamic so the navmesh rebuilds around moving obstacles
quiz.explain: By default the navmesh is static and built in the editor.

quiz.q: Why does a level designer do this walk test early?
choices: To check the route works for AI before building encounters in later quests
quiz.explain: Encounter spaces in later quests need AI that can actually get to the player.

quiz.q: What counts as 2 Blueprint interacts for this capstone?
choices: Two copies of the same door
Two different interactions, like a key-locked door and a lever-driven gate
quiz.explain: They must be different mechanics, each doing a job in a beat.

quiz.q: Your playtester got lost in the tension beat. What does the work you send need?
choices: The notes, what you changed in response, and an updated beat chart
quiz.explain: The capstone is about iterating. Show the change and why you made it.

quiz.q: How long can the video clip that you send be?
quiz.explain: Short clips get reviewed. If your level takes longer to play, cut between the beats, or send one screenshot per beat.

quiz.q: A reviewer spots a gap the character can't clear. Which document should have prevented it?
quiz.explain: Gaps and ledges come from your measured metrics, with margin.

quiz.q: Who approves this capstone?
choices: A peer or mentor, after the quiz
quiz.explain: This capstone is checked with the quiz plus the work you send, approved by a person.

quiz.q: Who approves this capstone?
choices: A mentor, or two peer approves
quiz.explain: Capstones at this level are reviewed by people, not by the quiz.

quiz.q: What must the before/after show?
choices: The same view before and after a change made from critique, with the feedback that led to it
quiz.explain: Same bookmark, one real change, and the feedback that prompted it.

quiz.q: The GDD says 'three enemies flank' but your build has no flank route. What do you do before you send your work?
choices: Fix the build or update the GDD so they match
quiz.explain: Reviewers check the build against the doc. They must agree.

quiz.q: Does this capstone need any C++?
choices: No. Blueprint, layout and docs only
quiz.explain: Level designers are never gated on C++.

quiz.q: What does the top-down map need to show?
choices: Nothing, a plain screenshot is fine
Entry, exit, cover, flanks, high ground and spawn points, labeled
quiz.explain: The annotated map is how a reviewer understands the space before they watch the clip.

quiz.q: Do you have to install Visual Studio to finish this quest?
choices: No, this quest is only reading
Only if you are a programmer
quiz.explain: This quest only asks you to read and understand. Visual Studio, the program used to write C++, is installed later in the Programming path.

quiz.q: Which of these is a normal reason to write something in C++ and not in Blueprint?
choices: It needs a lot of performance, or it is a core system that many Blueprints build on
quiz.explain: Heavy work and core systems go in C++. Content, and values you want to adjust quickly, stay in Blueprint.

quiz.q: Can a Blueprint be built on top of a class that was written in C++?
choices: Yes. A common setup is a C++ base class with Blueprint children
quiz.explain: Yes, and it is very common: programmers write the base in C++, and designers make Blueprint versions of it. It is also a capstone later in the Programming path.

quiz.q: Why do designers like to work in Blueprint?
choices: They can try changes quickly and see the logic as a graph, without compiling C++
It runs faster in the game
quiz.explain: In Blueprint you change something and test it right away. That speed of trying things is the reason Blueprint exists.

quiz.q: You chose Level Design as your specialization. After this quest, how much C++ do you still have to do?
choices: Rewrite your work in C++ in later quests
One small taster (a C++ hello or a GAS video), and nothing is locked behind it
quiz.explain: Level designers only do one short taster from the other side. They never have to rewrite their work in C++.

quiz.q: What does UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere) on a variable do?
choices: Makes it save to a text file
Shows it in the Details panel so it can be edited on the class defaults and on placed instances
quiz.explain: That's how a programmer gives designers a tuning knob.

quiz.q: What is the .h file for, compared with the .cpp?
choices: .h declares the class and its members; .cpp holds the function bodies
quiz.explain: Header declares, source implements. You'll mostly read headers to see what's exposed.

quiz.q: Which macro lets a C++ function be called from Blueprint?
quiz.explain: BlueprintCallable makes the function show up as a node.

quiz.q: A property is marked VisibleAnywhere. What do you see in Details?
choices: The value, but you can't change it there
quiz.explain: Visible means read-only in Details. EditAnywhere means editable.

quiz.q: Do you have to compile C++ to finish this taster?
choices: No. Compiling is an optional bonus; reading and finding the property is the task
Only if you want to become a programmer
quiz.explain: This taster is about reading C++, not setting up a toolchain.

quiz.q: What belongs under 'Goal' in an encounter GDD?
choices: One sentence on what the player should feel or learn
quiz.explain: One clear goal lets you judge every other choice against it.

quiz.q: Which is a player verb?
quiz.explain: Verbs are actions the player takes: move, shoot, flank, hide, pull.

quiz.q: Why list tuning knobs with current values?
choices: It makes the doc look long
So you and others know what to change and what it was before
quiz.explain: When a playtest goes badly, the knob list is where you look first.

quiz.q: Why keep the GDD to one page?
choices: It forces you to choose what matters, and reviewers actually read it
quiz.explain: A short doc gets read. A long one gets skimmed.

quiz.q: What is a fail state?
choices: How the player can lose, and what happens next
quiz.explain: Say how they lose and where they restart. That shapes how hard you can make it.
